A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaGC research. Their complete text, tables, figures, algorithms and appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM pretraining experiments, downstream benchmark results, CLIP experiments, training costs and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen3-1.7B results and further two-shot baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: Equation 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same per-tensor clipping rule, EMA of clipped gradient norms, GlobalGC warm-up and optimizer integration. Testing Qwen3 does not alter AdaGC's procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4-en pretraining and the same downstream language benchmarks, alongside LAION-400M training and ImageNet evaluation for CLIP. Qwen3-1.7B adds a model configuration within retained data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds ZClip as an evaluated comparator on Qwen3-1.7B. Table 12 also brings SPAM, WeSaR-GlobalGC and ScaledEmbed-GlobalGC into the Llama-2 two-shot comparisons; their zero-shot comparisons already appeared in v2.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Qwen3-1.7B setup with QK-Norm, 19,000 steps over 160B tokens, sequence length 4,096 and learning rate 4.5e-3. Retained experiment settings remain unchanged. Table 12 newly labels the retained zero-shot block 'One-Shot', contradicting its caption and discussion; this does not reliably establish an actual protocol change.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a compatibility check asking whether AdaGC remains beneficial with architectural stabilization, comparing training dynamics on Qwen3 with QK-Norm enabled throughout. The existing initialization, warm-up, adaptivity/locality ablations and optimizer-state analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides explicit repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for the reported comparisons. The existing seed discussion and spike-score calculation are retained; ZClip's added EMA standard deviation describes its algorithm, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched existing scores remain unchanged. New Qwen3 results report 50.37% zero-shot accuracy versus 48.42% for both GlobalGC and ZClip, with 1 versus 54 and 8 loss spikes respectively. Added two-shot results include ScaledEmbed-GlobalGC outperforming AdaGC on Llama-2 1.3B, 48.36% versus 47.56% (Table 12).

T1.justification: The convergence analysis moves from Appendix F to Appendix G. Its assumptions, lemmas, proofs and O(1/sqrt(T)) guarantee are identical after whitespace and numbering normalization; the proposed method's mathematical definitions are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive per-tensor clipping, optimizer compatibility, communication efficiency and training stability. The conclusion still claims consistently zero spike scores despite the added nonzero Qwen3 result.

C2.justification: New Section 6 and Appendix A substantially qualify applicability: AdaGC targets detectable sporadic gradient outliers but may miss cumulative numerical drift and failures with statistically normal gradients. v3 explains why EMA adaptation can conceal drift and positions clipping as complementary to architectural and infrastructure remedies. It also expands the explanation of small AdamW epsilon sensitivity.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code location, PaddlePaddle/PaddleFleet under Research/AdaGC, absent from v2. Tables 9–10 and Appendix C document Qwen3's configuration and ZClip's smoothing factor 0.97 and z-score threshold 2.0. Existing implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds ZClip to related work and the method comparison table, alongside references supporting Qwen3, QK-Norm, epsilon sensitivity, low-precision failures and silent training errors. These extend the comparison and limitations context while retaining the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a limitations section and scope appendix, rewrites the generic impact statement, and updates acknowledgments, affiliations and conference front matter. Experimental paragraphs and appendix headings receive localized edits; most existing prose and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Qwen3 training-dynamics figure and expands comparison and hyperparameter tables for Qwen3, ZClip and two-shot results. Existing figures and tables are retained with some relocation; v2 Figures 7–15 become v3 Figures 8–16. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The Qwen3/ZClip and additional two-shot comparisons make the empirical assessment more informative, while Section 6 and Appendix A explain important failure boundaries missing from v2. The code pointer also helps reproducibility. These gains outweigh limited reporting problems: the conclusion retains its zero-spike claim despite Qwen3's residual spike, and Table 12 introduces a conflicting 'One-Shot' label.
